question.value: Characterise the physical conditions and innermost dusty torus properties of the deeply embedded source D1 in the luminous infrared galaxy II Zw 096 using JWST observations of gas-phase rovibrational H2O and CO bands and IR-to-submm SED modelling.

evidence.quote: We analyze JWST NIRSpec+MIRI/MRS observations of the infrared (IR) gas-phase molecular bands of the most enshrouded source (D1) within the interacting system and luminous IR galaxy II Zw 096.

evidence.loc: Appendix D: Molecular grid of models and fitting of emission lines
evidence.quote: The torus models (396) have NCO=1-4×1018 cm−2, Tdust=300-400 K and 12CO/13CO=50-70. The outflow models (243) have CO density of 2-8×106 cm−3, Tdust=300-400 K, 12CO/13CO=50-70 and velocity dispersion ranging from 200 to 240 km/s. The SF extended component models (243) have NCO=1-4×1019 cm−2, Tdust=300-400 K, 12CO/13CO=50-70 and a range of covering factors to produce the P-R asymmetry. The cold extended component models (81) is represented by a cold component with Tgas=20-40 K, illuminated by an IR source with Tdust=300-400 K and 12CO/13CO=50-70.

findings_qualitative.value: Rovibrational lines of H2O v2=1-0 (~5.3-7.2 µm) with P-branch in emission and R-branch in absorption, and 12CO v=1-0 (~4.45-4.95 µm) with both R- and P-branches in emission, are detected in II Zw 096-D1.

evidence.quote: We report the detection of rovibrational lines of H2O ν2=1-0 (∼5.3-7.2 µm) and 12CO ν=1-0 (∼4.45-4.95 µm) in D1. The CO band shows the R- and P-branches in emission and the spectrum of the H2O band shows the P-branch in emission and the R-branch in absorption.

findings_qualitative.value: Weak Q-branch C2H2 (13.7 µm) and HCN (14.02 µm) mid-IR molecular absorption bands and ALMA submm HCN-vibrational (4-3) 356.256 GHz emission are detected in D1, confirming a compact deeply embedded nucleus.

evidence.quote: We also detect relatively weak Q-branch C2H2 (13.7µm) and HCN (14.02µm) molecular absorption in D1 (Appendix C).

findings_qualitative.value: High-ionization coronal lines indicative of an AGN (such as [Si VI], [Ar V], [Ar VI], [Ne V], [Ne VI]) are not clearly detected in D1 due to the exceptionally high covering factor of the dusty torus.

claims.hypothesis: The gas-phase rovibrational H2O and CO bands in II Zw 096-D1 can disentangle multiple physical components in the spatially unresolved inner region.
claims.experiment: Fit the continuum-subtracted JWST/NIRSpec and MIRI-MRS spectra from 4.45 to 7.3 µm using a 4-component library of non-local, non-LTE radiative transfer models.
claims.result: The bands are reproduced by four distinct components: a warm compact dusty torus (T_dust ~ 370 K, diameter ~ 1.4 pc at 5 µm) seen in H2O R-branch absorption, a highly turbulent outflow component (V_disp ~ 155 km/s) forming a broad CO plateau and broad H2O P-branch emission, an extended star-forming PDR component ([CO]/[H2O] ~ 100, V_disp ~ 35 km/s) showing rotation in CO P(13), and a cold extended gas component (T_gas ~ 20 K).
claims.finding: The H2O and CO bands successfully disentangle four physical components in D1, revealing an IR-bright embedded core connected to a turbulent environment alongside widespread circumnuclear PDRs.

evidence.quote: The detected H2O and CO bands demonstrate a great potential for disentangling different components, specifically, four in the case of D1.

By comparing the observed molecular rovibrational bands with radiative transfer models, we find that D1 is a complex structure featuring an IR-bright embedded dusty core (i.e. torus), which is most likely connected to a highly turbulent environment.

claims.hypothesis: Including the 4.5-7.0 µm continuum constraints inferred from H2O and CO rovibrational band modelling breaks multi-component SED fitting degeneracies and constrains the torus contribution.
claims.experiment: Perform MCMC SED fitting of the 1-850 µm SED (JWST, ALMA, Herschel) with CYGNUS dusty torus and star-forming models both with and without the 4.9-7.0 µm continuum derived from the H2O and CO band analysis.
claims.result: Without molecular band priors, the torus model overestimates the 4.9-7.0 µm intrinsic continuum (F_7µm^torus ~ 70%), which would produce deep absorption bands not observed; with the priors, F_7µm^torus drops to ~40% and the derived torus bolometric luminosity is about nine times smaller.
claims.finding: Modelling IR molecular bands provides a crucial observational limit on the inner dusty torus continuum level and overcomes SED multi-component fitting degeneracies.

evidence.quote: The torus continuum level is indeed constrained by the observed H 2 O absorption band. This provides an observational limit to the contribution of the torus.

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: We repeated the fitting process but including the 4.9-7.0 µm SED derived from the H2O and CO analysis (Fig. 4, left). The fractional contribution of the torus to the SED is lower (Ftorus 7µm ∼40%), and the derived torus bolometric luminosity is about nine times smaller.

claims.hypothesis: The deeply embedded source II Zw 096-D1 is powered by a buried dust-obscured AGN rather than a compact starburst.
claims.experiment: Derive the size, dust temperature, bolometric luminosity, and IR surface brightness of the D1 dusty core from the molecular-band-constrained torus SED model and compare with theoretical maximal starburst limits and proto-super star clusters.
claims.result: The torus is very compact (diameter ~3 pc at 5 µm and ~11 pc at 1 mm) with warm dust (~370 K), bolometric luminosity ~6.8x10^10 L_sun, and IR surface brightness ~3.6x10^8 L_sun/pc^2, which is ~36 times above the theoretical maximal starburst limit (~10^7 L_sun/pc^2).
claims.finding: D1 harbours a compact, dust-obscured AGN with an exceptionally high covering factor that prevents direct detection of high-IP AGN emission lines or hard X-rays.

evidence.quote: The torus is very compact (diameter of ∼3 pc at 5 µm) and characterised by warm dust (∼ 370 K), giving an IR surface brightness of ∼3.6×108 L⊙/pc2. This result suggests the presence of a dust-obscured active galactic nucleus (AGN) in D1, which has an exceptionally high covering factor that prevents the direct detection of AGN emission.

evidence.loc: 5. Alternative ways of looking for AGN in D1
evidence.quote: In addition, from the theoretical point of view, there is a limit of ∼107 L⊙/pc2 for a maximal SB (e.g. Thompson et al. 2005; Pereira-Santaella et al. 2021).

why_this_data.value: JWST NIRSpec and MIRI/MRS provide unprecedented high angular and spectral resolution (R~1500-3500) across 1.0-28.1 µm needed to detect and resolve gas-phase rovibrational H2O and CO lines in extragalactic buried nuclei, complemented by high-resolution ALMA archival submm data to sample the cold/submm SED and HCN-vib (4-3) emission.

evidence.quote: The unprecedented combination of high angular and spectral resolution (R∼1500-3500) in the 1.0-28.1 µm range afforded by the JWST Near-IR Spectrograph (NIRSpec; Jakobsen et al. 2022; Böker et al. 2022) and MIRI ( Rieke et al. 2015; Wells et al. 2015; Wright et al. 2015) are key to investigating deeply embedded sources such as II Zw 096-D1.

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: To build the 1-850 µm SED of D1, we used the entire NIRSpec and MRS spectra (resampled to ∼100 points), high angular resolution ALMA archival data (Appendix A), and lower angular resolution far-IR fluxes from Herschel.

why_this_method.value: Combining radiative transfer torus SED models with the 4.5-7.0 µm continuum constraints inferred from non-LTE H2O and CO rovibrational band modelling breaks multi-component AGN+SF SED fitting degeneracies in distant luminous IR systems.

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: Their central region consists of a combination of AGN and an intense SF activity component (e.g. Martínez-Paredes et al. 2015; Herrero-Illana et al. 2017; Efstathiou et al. 2022). Thus, best-fit solutions might be subject to multi-component fitting degeneracies. Here, we use the radiative transfer CYprus models for Galaxies and their NUclear Spectra (CYGNUS) project (Efstathiou et al. 2022).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: SED fit without prior continuum constraints from the H2O and CO molecular bands (rejected because it yields F_7µm^torus ~ 70% which would produce very deep molecular absorption bands that are not observed).

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: The resulting fit has a high fractional contribution of the torus to the SED at 7 µm (Ftorus 7µm ∼70%). We can discard this scenario given that this strong central component would produce very deep absorption bands that are not observed in D1.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Compact maximal starburst or extreme top-heavy IMF starburst powering D1 (rejected because the IR surface brightness of ~3.6x10^8 L_sun/pc^2 exceeds the theoretical maximal starburst limit of ~10^7 L_sun/pc^2, and top-heavy IMF systems are unstable on short timescales of a few Myr).

evidence.loc: 5. Alternative ways of looking for AGN in D1
evidence.quote: In addition, from the theoretical point of view, there is a limit of ∼107 L⊙/pc2 for a maximal SB (e.g. Thompson et al. 2005; Pereira-Santaella et al. 2021). Although we cannot rule out the possibility of an extreme top-heavy initial mass function (IMF) SB, this is unlikely since these systems are not stable on short timescales of few Myr (see e.g. Pereira-Santaella et al. 2021).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Identification of the 1.43 µm emission line as [Si X] (rejected because [Si VI], which is typically 1.8 times brighter than [Si X] in AGN, is not detected).

evidence.loc: 5. Alternative ways of looking for AGN in D1
evidence.quote: An emission line at 1.43 µm coincides with the expected position of [Si X] (IP: 351.1 eV), but [Si VI] is not detected, which is typically brighter than [Si X] in AGN (1.8 times on average; Rodríguez-Ardila et al. 2011). This indicates that the emission line observed at 1.43µm is not likely to be related to [Si X].

limitations_admitted.value: The CO band is in emission in D1, which hides the CO absorption related to the main luminosity source and allows only a lower limit on the CO column density of the torus component.

evidence.quote: This is likely due to the CO broad plateau in emission, which is hiding the CO absorption related to the main luminosity source.

The CO band is in emission in D1, which is not favourable for a definitive estimation of the CO column density of the torus component (in absorption). Thus, we consider the CO column density of the torus a lower limit.

limitations_admitted.value: The molecular band model assumes a single-temperature blackbody for the dust, whereas the CYGNUS torus models account for temperature gradients across the dust, resulting in a factor of ~2 difference in the derived 5 µm size (1.4 pc vs 3 pc).

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: The size of the dusty structure at 5 µm derived from the torus model is roughly twice as large as that determined by the molecular bands fit. This difference arises from the torus models accounting for temperature gradients across the dust, whereas the model of molecular bands includes a single temperature blackbody.

limitations_admitted.value: The best-fit SED model underestimates the continuum emission at ~12-15 µm, likely due to standard Galactic dust grain composition assumptions in a sub-solar metallicity source.

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: The resulting fit in Fig. 4 (left) underestimates the continuum emission at ∼12-15µm.

evidence.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
evidence.quote: Torus models generally assume the standard Galactic mix of 53% silicates and 47% graphite, which might be different in lower metallicity systems.

limitations_admitted.value: Diffuse/translucent clouds and molecular cloud envelopes with FUV photodesorption are not included in the molecular band model, leaving residuals in low-J CO lines (J<3), H2O lines connected to v2=0 low-excitation levels, and an overestimation of CO R(4) to R(6) transitions by the cold extended model.

evidence.loc: Appendix F: Residuals of the best-fit model of the molecular bands
evidence.quote: The latter are detected in the submm (e.g. Neufeld et al. 2000, 2002; Plume et al. 2004), and are not included in this model. As a consequence the fitted cold extended model for reproducing the relatively low-J lines of the CO band is overestimating the ∼R(4) to R(6) transitions.
